audit.whatIsWrong: Level 6 and First item both read Dr. Mundo, while whys[4] says you own the level-6 disengage edge he cannot match.
audit.why: The packet chart gives Level 6 to Poppy, and the mirror audit has already flipped Level 6 and First item to Poppy in both layers on Dr. Mundo's side, keeping 2+ items his. Matching that keeps the two directions identical.
audit.corrected: Rows 4 and 5 flipped to Poppy in both layers with ratings raised; whys[5] rewritten so the text agrees with the row rather than still calling first item even.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldowns; the page tells you to trade 'on his cleaver cooldown' without saying that cooldown is 4 seconds.
audit.why: Infected Bonesaw is 4s — there is no meaningful gap to trade in, which changes the advice entirely. Heart Zapper is 17s and Maximum Dosage 120s flat; those are the real windows.
audit.corrected: 4s, 17s and 120s written into the cooldown block, dosFull[0], report[5] and mid.

audit.whatIsWrong: Goes Where He Pleases is missing from the entire page — his passive resists the first immobilizing effect that hits him, which means your E wall-stun simply does not land until it has been spent. That is the single most important interaction in the matchup. Separately, the page credits Infected Bonesaw with healing him in three places; Riot's text gives Q no heal at all.
audit.why: Riot's text: P resists the first immobilize, drops a cannister he can pick up to heal and reduce its cooldown, and gives him large health regen. W stores a portion of damage taken and heals a percentage of it on the burst. R heals a percent of missing health. Q is current-health damage plus a slow. So the sustain to anti-heal is W and R, and the stun to bait is the passive.
audit.corrected: The immobilize-resist written into dontsFull[0], the cooldown block, report[5], early and spikes[0]; the heal correctly attributed to Heart Zapper and Maximum Dosage instead of the cleaver.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing warned about the auto-attack reset.
audit.why: Blunt Force Trauma is an active slam on a 9s cooldown at rank 1 that opens his damage — the wind-up is the cue to step back, not the cast.

edits.before: Early Mundo is genuinely weak and heal-starved, and you have point-and-click tools he can't dodge. At level 2-3 with Q+E up, look to E him into the wall behind him for the stun, then Q to chunk a chunk of his max HP before his passive sustain matters. Dodge his Q cleaver where you can since it's his only real poke and his main heal source, and pop W to shrug the trade and out-trade his flat early damage. Don't over-extend chasing a cleaver-missed Mundo into his tower.
edits.after: Early Mundo is genuinely weak, and you have point-and-click tools he can't dodge — but his passive resists your FIRST immobilize, so the opening E wall-stun does nothing until it is spent. Bait it, then trade. Sidestep Infected Bonesaw where you can; it is 4s, so there is no real gap, and pop W to eat the poke and out-trade his flat early damage. Don't chase a cleaver-missed Mundo into his tower.

edits.before: This is your honest window of relevance, not dominance. Your Q max-HP damage and E wall-stun still hurt him before his regen ramps, and W lets you eat his cleaver poke and trade back. At 6 your R is a disrupt tool, not burst: use it to cancel his all-in, peel his E-empowered run, or tap-knock him out of his Q rhythm. Keep forcing short trades on his cleaver cooldown rather than long fights where his passive and R out-heal you.
edits.after: This is your honest window of relevance, not dominance. Your Q and E wall-stun still hurt him before his regen ramps, and W lets you eat the poke and trade back. At 6 your R is a disrupt tool, not burst: cancel his all-in or knock him out of range. His cleaver is only 4s, so stop waiting for a poke gap — trade in the 17s after Heart Zapper pops and get Grievous Wounds down before the long fights.

notes: The biggest gap: Goes Where He Pleases resists the first immobilizing effect that hits him, so a cold E wall-stun is simply refused — nothing on the page mentioned it. Second, Infected Bonesaw was credited with healing him in three places; Riot's text gives Q current-health damage and a slow, and the heals live on Heart Zapper (stored damage) and Maximum Dosage (percent missing health). Level 6 and First item flipped to Poppy to match the mirror's chart edit; note that our packet chart reads Skill for First item, so if mirror-fix.js prefers the packet, that row may need a second look. Following the mirror, I did not introduce any new percent-max-health claim about Hammer Shock — Riot's text does not support it.
